full_judgment:
This appeal under section 100 of the Code of Civil Procedure is directed against the judgment and decree passed by Subordinate Judge, Second Additional Court, Sylhet reversing the decision of the learned Munsif, Additional Court, Sylhet in a suit for declaration for title and recovery of khas possession on the suit land. 

 4. The defendant No. 1 contested the suit by presenting a written statement traversing all the allegations made in the plaint. In the written statement it is stated that the suit land appertained to Taluk No.702/29 Patta Md Afsar originally belonged to Obaidur Rahman Choudhury in Maliki right and the suit land had been recorded in Cadestral Survey plot No. 2941. It is specifically pleaded that Obaidul Rahman Chowdhury was in khas possession of the plot No.2943 and he settled the said plot No. 2943 to the defendant No. 1 35 years back at a rent of Taka 6 and the defendant has been possessing the same openly and adversely by growing paddy therein. It is also averred that he paid rent to the superior landlords and received Farogs (Rend receipts) from the landlords. It is further stated that the adjacent eastern plot of CS Dag No.2943 is CS Dag No.2828 which appertained to Taluk No.6299 Lal Mohammad and the said plot was purchased by the father of the plaintiffs. It is the further case of the defendant that during the Survey Settlement Operation the entire land of CS Dag No.2943 was recorded as settlement survey Dag No.389 in the name of the defendant No.1. The plea of limitation and adverse possession have been also taken by the defendant No. 1 in the written statement. 

 7. The learned trial judge held that the contesting defendant could not file any document in support of his contention as to title and ownership on the land of CS Dag No. 2943. The learned trial judge then recorded the finding that CS Dag No. 2943 was originally jungle kind of land which led him to believe that while the defendant No.1 had been possessing the CS Dag No. 2943 he cleared the jungle and amalgamated the suit land with his own land and the plaintiffs having found the suit land as good Boro land, they became alert and filed so many cases to get the land under their possession from the possession of the defendant but they could nowhere succeed. The learned trial judge was of the view that since it is not denied that the defendant has been possessing contiguous western land of the suit land for a long time, about 35 years, he was constrained to hold that he has been possessing the suit land for the last 35 years as contended by him. The learned trial judge was, also, of the view that the documentary evidence of possession of the defendant in the suit land has also shown that the defendant has been possessing the suit land since long time. The learned trial Judge ultimately came to the finding that the plaintiff''s title to the suit land became barred since the defendant has been in possession thereof adversely against the statutory period of limitation and the suit stands barred by limitation and the prayer of the plaintiffs for recovery of khas possession of the suit land is also not tenable. With the above finding and views the learned trial Judge dismissed the suit. 

 8. The plaintiffs carried an appeal against the said decision of the learned trial Judge to the Court of District Judge, Sylhet. The learned Subordinate Judge, Additional Second Court, Sylhet heard the appeal and concurred with the decision of the learned trial Judge on the question of title and held that the learned Munsif had rightly opined that the defendant No. 1 failed to prove title in the suit land by any cogent document. The learned Subordinate Judge believed the title deeds of the plaintiffs and arrived at the conclusion that the plaintiffs have right, title and interest in the disputed land and they acquired it from their father Khalilur Rahman by way of inheritance and by amicable arrangement with their other co-sharers. The learned Subordinate Judge held also, that when a properly framed title suit has been filed in respect of the same land and when the matter is under investigation in a civil court, the opinions and observation of the Revenue officer was not of much value for the determination of the dispute between the parties. The learned Subordinate Judge also recorded the finding that in the proceeding under section 145 of the Code of Criminal Procedure the possession of the disputed land was found with the First Party Nabibur Rahman Chowdhury (plaintiff No.1) and it was ordered that he would not be disturbed in his possession therein until evicted in due course of law and the Second party, the present defendant No. 1 having not filed a suit for recovery of khas possession within 3 years from the date of the order. The plaintiffs acquired a good title to the property under section 28 of the Limitation Act. The learned Subordinate Judge was of the view that the possibility of dispossession of the plaintiffs by the defendant No. 1 from the suit land after the judgment passed in favour but in view of the facts and circumstances of the case learned Subordinate Judge found that the plaintiff''s suit is not barred by Limitation and reversed the decision of the learned trial judge on the question of limitation allowed the appeal and decreed the suit.
